title: WHEN A BAD REPORT BEARS ITS FRUIT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will surely do these things to this whole wicked community, which has banded together against me. They will meet their end in this wilderness; here they will die. So the men Moses had sent to explore the land, who returned and made the whole community grumble against him by spreading a bad report about it — these men who were responsible for spreading the bad report about the land were struck down and died of a plague before the Lord. Of the men who went to explore the land, only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh survived. — Num 14:35-38 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The ten spies who spread the bad report die of a plague "before the Lord." Their fearful, faithless words had infected an entire nation and cost a generation the promise. Now they face the consequence of the discouragement they had sown. Words carry weight, and these men bore the heavy weight of theirs.

We must not miss the seriousness of this. The ten did not commit murder or theft; their sin was unbelief expressed in discouraging words. Yet God treated it gravely, because their words had turned a whole people away from trusting Him. What we say to others about God and His promises has real power — to build faith or to destroy it.

Set against the ten, two men stand: "only Joshua and Caleb survived." The same mission, the same giants, the same evidence — but a different spirit produced a different destiny. Faith and unbelief lead to profoundly different ends. God preserved the faithful two while the faithless ten fell.

This is a sober word, but it carries an invitation. We are always shaping others by our words — spreading a "bad report" of fear and complaint, or a good report of God's faithfulness. Which will we sow? The story urges us to be Joshuas and Calebs, whose trust in God strengthens everyone around them. And it points us to Christ, in whom the good report is finally and fully true: God is faithful, the promise is secure, and those who trust Him will not be put to shame.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do your words about God and His promises build others' faith or erode it?
2. Why does God take discouraging unbelief so seriously?
3. How can you be a Joshua or Caleb to those around you this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, make me one who spreads a good report of Your faithfulness rather than a bad report of fear. Help my words to strengthen the faith of others. Thank You that in Christ Your promises are certain and sure. Amen.
